ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the left energy band diagram, the vertical axis is labeled E(eV), and the horizontal axis is x; both the conduction band Ec and the valence band Ev slope downward as x increases, and the slope is explicitly labeled in the figure as -0.1 eV/cm. In the right figure, the vertical axis is log(n(x)), and the horizontal axis is x; the curve rises linearly as x increases, indicating that the electron concentration increases exponentially with x. Reasoning: From the conduction band slope in the figure, dEc/dx = -0.1 eV/cm, and according to the method specified in the problem, take the electric field E = -0.1 V/cm. The electron concentration is n(x)=10^15 exp[alpha x/(kT/q)], where alpha=0.1 V/cm, so dn/dx = n alpha/(kT/q). At x=0, n=10^15 cm^-3. The electron current density is Jn = q μn n E + q Dn dn/dx. From the Einstein relation Dn/μn = kT/q, μn = Dn/(kT/q). Therefore the drift term is q Dn n E/(kT/q) = q Dn n(-alpha)/(kT/q), and the diffusion term is q Dn n alpha/(kT/q). The two terms have equal magnitudes and opposite signs, canceling each other, so Jn(0)=0 A/cm^2.
